*PharmaCraft Daily - 15 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Low-dose aspirin is used for its effect on?
Ans: Platelet aggregation
Why: Low-dose aspirin irreversibly inhibits platelet COX-1, reducing thromboxane A2 and aggregation.

🌍 *FMGE* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Which drug is preferred for fever in children?
Ans: Paracetamol
Why: Paracetamol is the preferred antipyretic in children; aspirin is avoided.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Which drug is used for acute gout and inhibits neutrophil migration via microtubules?
Ans: Colchicine
Why: Colchicine binds tubulin, impairing neutrophil chemotaxis; effective in acute gout but GI toxicity limits dose.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad) results from?
Ans: Shunting of arachidonate to leukotrienes after COX inhibition
Why: COX inhibition diverts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes, causing bronchospasm in sensitive asthmatics.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: Which insulin has the fastest onset for prandial control?
Ans: Lispro/aspart (rapid-acting analogues)
Why: Rapid-acting analogues (lispro, aspart, glulisine) act within 15 minutes, ideal for mealtime coverage.
